knowledge:
- key_parameters: anno_col=The column name in colData containing cell type annotations, passed to readHoodData ;; k (in findNearCells)=The number of nearest neighbor cells to identify for each cell (e.g., k = 100) ;; k (in clustByHood)=The number of clusters to use for k-means clustering of neighborhood probability distributions ;; pm_cols=The column names of the neighborhood probability matrix (typically the cell types) used in downstream analysis and plotting functions ;; targetCells=A vector of specific cell IDs of interest to plot in plotHoodMat
- alternatives: None mentioned. The package uses the RANN package (Approximate Near Neighbor C++ library) internally for fast nearest neighbor searching.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have single-cell resolution spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., from platforms like CosMx, Xenium, or MERFISH) and want to characterize, visualize, and cluster the local cellular neighborhoods of individual cells.
- pitfalls: Ensure that the input SpatialExperiment object is properly formatted using readHoodData with the correct cell annotation column before running downstream neighborhood scanning functions.

workflows.name: cellular_neighborhood_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform cellular neighborhood scanning, colocalization analysis, and neighborhood-based clustering on single-cell spatial transcriptomics data.
input: spe (SpatialExperiment object containing single-cell spatial transcriptomics data with cell type annotations and spatial coordinates)
workflows.stages: 1. Format the SpatialExperiment input object using readHoodData ;; 2. Visualize cell positions and annotations using plotTissue ;; 3. Identify nearest neighbor cells using findNearCells ;; 4. Calculate neighborhood association probabilities using scanHoods ;; 5. Merge probabilities by cell type groups using mergeByGroup ;; 6. Visualize neighborhood probabilities using plotHoodMat ;; 7. Merge neighborhood results back into the SpatialExperiment object using mergeHoodSpe ;; 8. Calculate neighborhood entropy and perplexity using calcMetrics and visualize them using plotTissue ;; 9. Perform neighborhood colocalization analysis using plotColocal ;; 10. Cluster cells by neighborhood probability distribution using clustByHood ;; 11. Visualize cluster probability distributions using plotProbDist and spatial clusters using plotTissue
workflows.code:
spe <- readHoodData(spe, anno_col = "celltypes")
plotTissue(spe, color = cell_annotation, size = 1.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = col.pal)
fnc <- findNearCells(spe, k = 100)
pm <- scanHoods(fnc$distance)
hoods <- mergeByGroup(pm, fnc$cells)
plotHoodMat(hoods, n = 10, hm_height = 5)
plotHoodMat(hoods, targetCells = c("Lung9_Rep1_5_1975", "Lung9_Rep1_5_2712"), hm_height = 3)
spe <- mergeHoodSpe(spe, hoods)
spe <- calcMetrics(spe, pm_cols = colnames(hoods))
plotTissue(spe, size = 1.5, color = entropy) +
  scale_color_scico(palette = "tokyo")
plotTissue(spe, size = 1.5, color = perplexity) +
  scale_color_scico(palette = "tokyo")
plotColocal(spe, pm_cols = colnames(hoods))
spe <- clustByHood(spe, pm_cols = colnames(hoods), k = 10)
plotProbDist(spe, pm_cols = colnames(hoods), by_cluster = TRUE, plot_all = TRUE, show_clusters = as.character(seq(10)))
plotTissue(spe, color = clusters)
